serves_registry_rows: presence.people (share of persons in each of six states, by day type and clock hour)
attach.phone.network (a bracket from places, not a measurement of networks)

sources.name: American Time Use Survey, multi-year microdata 2003-2024 (diary years 2022-2024 for the table; 2015-2019 beside it)
sources.notice: Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, American Time Use Survey, 2003-2024 multi-year microdata files. A derived work; not endorsed by the Bureau.

keys.unit: a person aged 15 or over; one diary day each
keys.day_type: Monday to Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday; hours after midnight carry the next day's name
keys.value: weighted mean share of the hour's minutes in each state; the six sum to 1

envelope.place: no geography; metropolitan and non-metropolitan respondents differ by 0.015 on average in the at-home share and by up to 0.07 in an hour

errors: a weighted bootstrap over respondents; the survey's replicate weights give 0.95 of it at the median, so it is not understated

verdict.twin_at_work_8_to_18_everyone: a reading: at most 0.51 of the employed are at a workplace at once (Monday to Thursday), above half that peak from 7 to 17
verdict.twin_on_wifi_0.65: inside the bracket 0.61 to 0.79 of awake time (at home; at home or at a workplace or school): a statement about places, not networks
verdict.one_table_for_town_and_country: untestable at this budget: 4 of 96 cells have errors small enough to carry a verdict
verdict.rows_by_age_and_employment_predict_house: untestable at this budget: 6 of 288 cells

limits: one person per household: whether anyone is home is measured only for one-person households; otherwise the 'household' block is a bracket
a person awake is not a device awake
9.1 % of sleep minutes had no located episode in their segment and are at home by default
the regime moved: the at-home share 9 to 17 on working days was 0.414 in 2015-2019 and 0.501 in 2022-2024
